records.claimSummary: The gateway checks the caller's access token with the auth service and routes the request to the right service.
records.conditionSummary: If the auth service cannot be reached, the gateway rejects the request (fails closed) rather than letting it through.
records.mustConvey: auth service unreachable -> request rejected (not let through unchecked)
records.bindingReason: When the auth service is unreachable the gateway does not route the request at all, so 'checks the token and routes the request' is misleading for that case.

records.claimSummary: The gateway applies a rate limit.
records.conditionSummary: The rate limit is 120 requests per minute per account.
records.bindingReason: 'The gateway applies a rate limit' stays true without the value; the bound is a specification that must appear somewhere.
records.notes: Intra-sentence bound; could be argued claim-binding if a card stated a different scope (e.g. global).

records.claimSummary: Every client request enters through the API gateway.
records.conditionSummary: Photo bytes are served to clients by the CDN, never by the gateway.
records.mustConvey: photo bytes served by the CDN, never by the gateway
records.bindingReason: For photo/thumbnail loads the traffic goes to the CDN, so 'every client request enters through the gateway' would be read as covering photo bytes and be false.
records.notes: u7 (direct upload to object storage) is a second exception of the same kind; u2_n19 / u4_n4 convey it.

records.claimSummary: Clients upload photos directly to object storage with a signed URL.
records.bindingReason: Direct upload via signed URL is still true without 'short-lived'; it is a security property that should appear somewhere.
records.notes: Borderline adjective vs. condition; kept because it is the only limit on the signed URL's validity. u2_n19 conveys it only via the appended 'From the source: short-lived' fragment.

records.claimSummary: The upload service and workers only meet through the message queue so a slow/failed thumbnail job never blocks or fails an upload.
records.conditionSummary: Cost: a new photo takes a few seconds to appear in feeds.
records.mustConvey: a few seconds' delay before a new photo appears in feeds
records.bindingReason: The queue decision and its benefit stay true; the delay is the accepted cost that must be recorded somewhere.

records.claimSummary: A worker outage delays thumbnails but does not lose uploads.
records.conditionSummary: Because the queue keeps an event for up to 7 days.
records.bindingReason: An outage longer than 7 days would lose events, so 'does not lose uploads' is false beyond the retention bound.

records.claimSummary: In the posting flow the worker creates thumbnails, marks the photo ready, and the feed service adds it to followers' feeds.
records.conditionSummary: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays 'processing' and is never shown in any feed.
records.mustConvey: repeatedly failing processing -> stays 'processing', not shown in feeds
records.bindingReason: For a photo whose processing keeps failing, the flow's outcome (photo distributed to followers' feeds) does not happen, so an unconditional reading of the flow is false.
records.notes: u3_a2 ('the entire flow ensures that a user's photo is ... distributed to followers' feeds') is the clearest claim card. The source flow is sequential, so binding could be argued 'set' for u32 alone.

records.claimSummary: The feed service keeps ready-made feed pages in the cache.
records.conditionSummary: Feed pages are cached for 60 seconds.
records.bindingReason: Caching feed pages stays true without the TTL; the 60 s staleness bound must appear somewhere.

records.claimSummary: Clients send photo bytes straight to object storage; routing through the gateway would make it the bottleneck.
records.conditionSummary: Originals can be up to 25 MB (the deciding fact).
records.bindingReason: The direct-upload decision stays true without the size; the 25 MB figure is the deciding fact that should appear somewhere.

records.claimSummary: Pinhole uses a third-party CDN and push-notification provider instead of running its own.
records.conditionSummary: We accept that their outages are outside our control.
records.mustConvey: third-party outages are outside Pinhole's control
records.bindingReason: The buy decision stays true; the accepted risk is a caveat that must be recorded somewhere.

records.claimSummary: The feed service asks the push-notification provider to alert followers.
records.conditionSummary: Pinhole only sends requests and does not control when an alert arrives.
records.mustConvey: Pinhole does not control alert delivery timing
records.bindingReason: 'Asks the provider to alert' stays true; the lack of control over timing is a caveat.

records.claimSummary: Followers are alerted (via the push-notification provider) when a photo is ready.
records.conditionSummary: Only followers who have notifications turned on are alerted.
records.mustConvey: only followers with notifications turned on
records.bindingReason: Followers with notifications off are not alerted, so 'alerts followers' is false for them.
records.notes: Source u32 itself drops the scope; u3_n8 follows u32.

records.claimSummary: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays in the 'processing' state.
records.conditionSummary: How failed processing is retried and when a stuck photo is cleaned up is not decided yet.
records.mustConvey: retry and cleanup of stuck photos undecided
records.bindingReason: The stuck-state statement stays true; the open question is a caveat that must be recorded somewhere.

notes: No records for u1-u6 (purpose, scope, client description), u21/u22/u36 (facts and rationale, not limits), u25/u26/u28 (boundary facts), u29/u30/u33 (flow steps without conditions), u37 (rationale - 'because' clause, a cause), u40 (deferred feed precompute, an open question with no limited claim), u13 'once the upload completes' (timing detail, judged minor). Decision-title shapes (u4_n1/u4_n3/u4_n9) were treated as claim cards since their visible text names the decision; they are linked to their detail text. Component-label shapes in g1 (e.g. 'Cache', 'API Gateway') were not treated as claim cards. Group-to-group arrows (g1 -> g2 etc.) were not counted as linking individual cards.
